To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of human CYP2C isoforms in Escherichiacoli requires the use of an appropriate expression construct and that the co-expression of CYP2Cs with NADPH-P450 reductase in the same membrane is more effective than the addition of exogenous reductase.

the co-expression of cytochrome P-450 and NADPH-cyt P-450 reductase in Escherichiacoli is a complex process and that the optimal expression conditions for each cytochrome P -450 isoform must be determined.

the co-expression of human cytochromep450 (P450) 2C9 with its NADPH-cytocrome P450 reductases (OxR), using a bicistronic expression vector, resulted in the expression of low amounts of the OxR and, consequently, low P450 activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of bacterial expression of human CYP2C enzymes, with a focus on CYP2C19, which is of particular interest due to the polymorphism of this enzyme.
the expression of human cytochroms P450 (Cyp450) and the development of an efficient expression system to produce active enzymes.
the expression of human P450s and the development of a catalytically competent system for the study of the P450 isoform, CYP2C.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most efficient expression of Cyp2C8 and CyP2C9 in E. coli is achieved by co-expression of CYP2c8 or CYP2C 9 and OxR with the A3 -20 construct and that the most efficient reconstitution of CYP2 9 activity is achieved by co-expressing the CYP2C and OxR in the same membrane.

the most effective approach to produce a catalytic active human P450 system is to co-express CYP and OxReductase in the same cell using an expression construct that gives the highest expression level of the CYP isoform.
the best approach to obtain a catalytically-active CYP2C system depends on the P450 isoform.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CYP:OXR fusion protein is a good strategy, but the N-terminal modification of CYP is important to achieve high catalytic activity.

the A3- 20 construct for Cyp2C9, the 17a-leaders for CYP2B6, CYP2C18, CYP2E1, and CYP4A11, and the A3-15 construct for CYP3A4, all with co-expression of OxR in the same membrane, give catalytically active bacterial systems with Km and Vmax values similar to human microsomes for a range of substrates.
the 17a-leaders for the CYP2C subfamily and A3-20 for the CYP3A subfamily are the best N-terminal presequences for expression of catalytily active CYPs in Escherichiia coli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no universal approach to expressing human cytochrome p450s.
the choice of expression construct and co-expression strategy should not be generalized to all P450s but should be individualized.
there is no single optimal approach to the co-expression of P450 and NADPH-cyclochrome P450 reudctase in Escherichio coli.
